title: I Think I Turned My Childhood Friend Into a Girl
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Popular high schooler Kenshirou Midou secretly loves cosmetics and practices makeup on his small, plain childhood friend Hiura. Hiura enjoys the feminine look, starts wearing the girls' uniform to school, and the two boys realize they are attracted to each other (Seven Seas blurb via AniList; Wikipedia).
life_message: Being free to present yourself as you like, and to love regardless of gender, makes people happier and more themselves.

content.note: Romance between two boys, one cross-dressing (AniList Boys' Love 87; MU Shounen Ai); MangaDex rates it safe.
Kenshirou hides his hobby from almost everyone (AniList blurb).
Makeup and fashion tips; nothing risky.

dominant: Gender expression; love regardless of gender; hidden hobbies

frames.aligns: Kenshirou and Hiura's long friendship and kindness to each other.
frames.concerns: Hiura's cross-dressing and the boys' romance run against Church teaching on sex and gender.
Gender seen as given; cross-dressing and same-sex attraction celebrated.

frames.aligns: Friendship and honesty about a hidden hobby.
frames.concerns: Cross-dressing (Deut. 22:5) and same-sex romance presented positively.

frames.aligns: Accepting a friend as he is.
frames.concerns: Gender expression and same-sex attraction as liberation.

frames.aligns: Friendship and talent in a craft.
frames.concerns: Conservative churches object to cross-dressing romance; PC(USA) differs.

frames.aligns: Love of neighbor; ELCA families more open.
frames.concerns: LCMS and WELS object to gender-bending romance.
Holiness and Global Methodist families object.

frames.aligns: Dignity of every person, as the Episcopal Church holds.

frames.concerns: Plain-dress communities object to cross-dressing and same-sex romance.

frames.concerns: English vol. 1 mislabeled Hiura as trans (Wikipedia).
Men imitating women and same-sex attraction are central.

frames.aligns: Gender fluidity has some places in Hindu tradition.
No harm, kindness and honesty between friends.
Gender expression and queer romance shown warmly.

frames.concerns: Gender nonconformity and same-sex romance aimed at teens.
Cross-dressing and same-sex romance are the premise.

frames.aligns: Freedom from fear of others' judgment.
Worth and dignity of a gender-nonconforming teen.
Freedom to be oneself, affirming of queer love.
Sincerity and beauty; cross-dressing has stage traditions in Japan.

frames.concerns: Traditional teaching on marriage; diaspora varies.
Sexual relations limited to man-woman marriage.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No face-saving conflict noted; light comedy (AniList).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Hiura chooses to wear the girls' uniform to school (AniList blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Kenshirou practices on his sisters before Hiura (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Gender norms set aside for personal choice.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Makeup and dress as liberating self-expression (AniList blurb).

folkways.japan: Hiura fits the Japanese 'otokonoko' (feminine-presenting boy) type, a fashion and fiction category distinct from transgender identity (Wikipedia; MU).

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia reception focuses on Hiura's cuteness and love 'regardless of gender'; no review calls it preachy (to verify).
delivery.note: The theme is carried by the two boys' daily life and feelings; sources mention no character arguing the other side.

winners_losers: Hiura and Kenshirou grow closer and freer; sources name no losers. Sympathy goes to self-expression.
